branches.label: Follow the encounter accounts

character.centerRule: Paul of Tarsus remains distinct from King Saul. Acts narration, the thirteen in Scripture Paul-named letters, and 2 Peter’s later memory retain their own voice, audience, sequence, and limits; Hebrews is not assigned to Paul.

phases.orientation: Saul first appears beside Stephen’s death and the scattering that follows, then carries threats toward Damascus.
phases.title: Saul, witness and opponent

phases.orientation: A light, a voice, blindness, Ananias, baptism, first proclamation, danger, and contested reception change Saul’s direction.
phases.title: Encounter and first witness

phases.orientation: Barnabas retrieves Saul, Antioch becomes a sending community, and Paul moves through Cyprus and southern Galatia with changing audiences and resistance.
phases.title: Antioch and the first mission

phases.orientation: A Jerusalem dispute, a mission partnership rupture, new coworkers, imprisonment, and public reasoning carry the work toward Corinth.
phases.title: Council and the second journey

phases.orientation: Teaching, signs, public conflict, farewell speech, warnings, and determined travel gather around Paul’s return toward Jerusalem.
phases.title: Ephesus and the road to Jerusalem

phases.orientation: Paul enters Jerusalem, is seized, addresses crowds and council, and repeatedly narrates identity, encounter, calling, and hope under custody.
phases.title: Arrest and testimony

phases.orientation: Hearings before governors and a king lead to appeal, storm, shipwreck, Malta, Rome, and an open-ended final witness.
phases.title: Trials, voyage, and Rome

phases.orientation: Romans moves through gospel, judgment, faith, Adam, baptism, law, Spirit, Israel, embodied practice, disputed food, mission, and named coworkers.
phases.title: Gospel, Israel, and shared life

phases.orientation: The Corinthian letters expose division, bodies, meals, gifts, resurrection, weakness, reconciliation, generosity, authority, suffering, and defense.
phases.title: Corinth and contested apostleship

phases.orientation: Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, and Philemon hold autobiography, freedom, one body, imprisonment, coworkers, and reconciliation together.
phases.title: Freedom, unity, and imprisonment letters

phases.orientation: The Thessalonian and pastoral letters speak through memory, absence, leadership, teaching, endurance, household order, coworkers, and approaching death.
phases.title: Communities, suffering, and final charge

phases.orientation: A later letter names Paul as a beloved brother whose letters require patient and careful reading.
phases.title: Later Scripture memory

character.throughline: Saul appears beside Stephen’s death, is confronted on the Damascus road, becomes known as Paul, moves through mission and custody, speaks through letters to particular communities and coworkers, and is later remembered as a beloved brother whose letters require care.
